page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-2 is a general-purpose server instance configured with 2 vCPUs and 8 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server features 1 physical core with 2 threads per core and dedicated CPU allocation. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 33 MB L3 cache, alongside hardware support for AVX-512 vector extensions, AES cryptography, and Intel Virtualization Technology. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tier for compute-heavy and memory-intensive tasks. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 1398.19 is in the bottom 25%, while the multi-core score of 1837.38 falls into the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block transfers measured at 13.8 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 11.79 GB/sec, both ranking in the bottom 10%. However, single-threaded gzip compression shows average performance at 23.81 GB/sec.

From a resource density perspective, the server offers a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for entry-level workloads that do not require high throughput. Tradeoffs include poor multi-core scaling, low database operation scores of 731.04 on PassMark, and a static web serving throughput of 1.95 GB/sec. It is best suited for lightweight general-purpose applications, basic text processing, and simple web serving rather than data-intensive or high-concurrency tasks.
